original.disposition: Consume the initial batch: the refined two-step solve is a solver-grid solution only. Its unsoftened holding speed sits at 98.7% of the 0.02 m/s limit while its independent BDF replay shows 0.043122 m/s holding speed and 2.449 mm node tip disagreement, so replay gates fail and no trustworthy feasible schedule exists. Among the permitted levers, substeps is already at its maximum (2), the position/speed weights are inert because the gap term is identically zero at the returned slack-zero point, and a design change targets a different question (d=0 already reaches NLP-grid feasibility and historically beat d=0.767). The only lever that can select a better-margined member of this degenerate slack-zero feasible set is the secondary effort/variation regularizer, so I request ONE revision solve with objective_mode task_gap_with_effort, secondary_coefficient at its allowed maximum 0.001, everything else unchanged (d=0 frozen, weights 1.0/1.0, substeps 2, warm start from the just-returned candidate), plus its one independent BDF replay. Then STOP.

original.hypothesis: The returned refined-grid point is one arbitrary member of a degenerate optimal set, which is why its speed margin is razor-thin. Evidence: at substeps=2 the solve reports hard_max_normalized_violation 9.99e-9 with slack_values position/speed both about -1e-8 (pinned at their zero bound, so effectively unused), original_task_gaps position 0.0 and speed 0.0, and selected_search_objective -1.998e-08, i.e. the gap objective is identically zero at that point, so it cannot prefer any slack-zero feasible point over another and the iterate lands at 98.7% of the holding-speed limit (0.019742 vs 0.02 m/s). Secondary effort/variation regularization is the only permitted mechanism that gives the search a preference inside that feasible set; with coefficient 0.001 it stays far below the unit slack penalty (so slacks should remain zero) while rewarding lower-amplitude, smoother tension histories, which plausibly restores holding-speed margin and thereby reduces the continuum-versus-grid bias that dominates the replay error (speed 0.0466 m/s versus tip 2.46 mm).
limitations: This will be the second and final full NLP attempt; if it returns no usable schedule, no further solve is available.

original.revision_or_stop_rule: This is the single revision batch. After consuming its solve and independent replay: (a) if the returned schedule keeps slack at zero and the replay meets both gates (node/dense tip disagreement under 1 mm, speed disagreement under 0.002 m/s) with unsoftened holding/terminal position under 0.01 m and holding speed under 0.02 m/s, report that bounded numerical result as the outcome and STOP; (b) if the replay still exceeds a gate or the unsoftened limits, record the two-candidate comparison (original grid versus refined grid, with and without effort regularization) as the result and STOP, with no further solve; (c) if the revision returns only failure or unusable output, interpret that honestly and STOP. original.weakening_observation: The refinement did not buy acceptance. Solving the frozen-design slack problem on the refined two-step grid moved the iterate to a point that is unsoftened-feasible on the solver grid (holding position 0.005515 m, terminal 0.005515 m, holding speed 0.019742 m/s, all inside limits, slack effectively zero) but its independent BDF replay exceeds both replay gates: node_max_tip_disagreement 0.002449 m and node_max_speed_disagreement 0.030684 m/s (dense 0.002460 m and 0.046612 m/s), gates_passed false, and the replay's own holding speed is 0.043122 m/s (sampled evaluator 0.037135 m/s), roughly double the 0.02 m/s task limit. The same comparison on the original grid was 0.008106 m and 0.0997 m/s, so refinement helps but remains far outside gates, and the returned point has essentially no speed margin (0.019742 versus 0.02, about 1.3% headroom). This weakens any claim that solver-grid feasibility transfers to the continuous model at the maximum permitted refinement.

Its independent BDF replay fails both acceptance gates: node tip disagreement 0.002449 m and node speed disagreement 0.030684 m/s (dense 0.002460 m / 0.046612 m/s), gates_passed false, with replayed holding speed 0.043122 m/s (sampled evaluator 0.037135 m/s) — about 2.2x the 0.02 m/s limit, while position metrics replayed at 0.005423 m, inside 0.01 m. The single permitted revision (add effort/variation regularization at the allowed maximum secondary coefficient 0.001) effectively refuted my revision hypothesis: the retained candidate moved by only about 0.1 mm in holding position and about 0.6 mm/s in solver-grid holding speed (0.005407 m, 0.019154 m/s, effort 0.252121, slacks +5.06e-07) and its replay changed by under 0.2% (node tip 0.002453 m, node speed 0.030600 m/s, dense 0.002463 m / 0.046429 m/s, gates_passed false, replayed holding speed 0.042181 m/s), so the boundary-hugging solver-grid point is not a regularization artifact or a warm-start artifact, and the solver also hit Maximum_CpuTime_Exceeded (34 iterations, 572.06 s of a 600 s budget, hard violation 5.53e-06, still inside the 1e-05 hard tolerance, retained export at iteration 3). Net conclusion: refinement improved solver-versus-continuum agreement relative to the pre-existing original-grid evidence (0.008106 m tip / 0.0997 m/s speed) by roughly a factor of three, but both limits remain exceeded and no schedule satisfies the replay gates or the unsoftened holding-speed limit in independent integration, so no task success is claimed. Weight search was excluded on evidence rather than on preference: the gap term is identically zero at the retained slack-zero point, so position/speed weights within [0.25,4] cannot reorder or improve the solver-grid solution, and design search was excluded because d=0 already attains solver-grid feasibility and the historical d>0 point was worse.

(H2) the degenerate gap-only objective selects an arbitrary slack-zero feasible point, so the maximum-permitted effort/variation regularization could buy holding-speed margin — refuted: adding secondary_coefficient 0.001 changed the retained solution and its replay by well under one percent (holding speed 0.019742 to 0.019154 m/s solver-grid, replayed 0.043122 to 0.042181 m/s) and did not change the failure, so the boundary-hugging speed is intrinsic to the refined-grid model rather than an artifact of objective degeneracy or of the warm start taken from the diagnosed original-grid iterate.

Weights were not varied, but this is an evidence-based exclusion, not a completeness claim: the gap term is identically zero at the retained point, so weight changes within [0.25,4] could alter the objective by at most about 4x5e-07.

Slacks are search-only: the initial slack sat at the zero bound and the revision slack was +5.06e-07, both negligible, but a relaxed feasible iterate is not by itself task success and the acceptance criteria were evaluated on unsoftened metrics.

original.weakening_observation: What weakened the case for feasibility: after the maximum permitted refinement and the strongest permitted selection lever, the replayed holding speed is still roughly double the limit (0.043122 m/s initial, 0.042181 m/s revision, versus 0.02 m/s) and replay disagreement barely improved (node tip 0.002449 to 0.002453 m, node speed 0.030684 to 0.030600 m/s), i.e. the effort/variation regularizer at its ceiling bought essentially nothing.
